no_systemd:
No background service was installed: this computer has no usable systemd user service ({error}). Use another way to keep persona-link running:
  · Start it in the background now:
      nohup {run} >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  · Start it at boot with cron:
      (crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '@reboot {run} >/dev/null 2>&1') | crontab -
  · On a NAS such as Synology, add a user script triggered at boot in Task Scheduler, using the nohup line above (run as this user, not root).
  · In a container, make {run} the main process with restart policy unless-stopped, mount ~/.persona as a volume (it contains the credentials), and run the resident node in the same container.
  · With a process manager such as supervisord, runit, s6, or OpenRC, run the command above in the foreground and restart it when it exits.
Once running, use persona-link status for status and persona-link logs -f for logs.

usage:
Usage:
  persona-link pair [--machine <id>] [--ssh <server> [--ssh-target <address:port>] [--ssh-always|--no-ssh-always]] [--proxy <url>] [<pairing link>|-]
                                                 Active mode (connect to the hub): pair with a link from personad hub pair; credentials go in
                                                 ~/.persona/link.json. With no link, or -, read it from standard input (a terminal prompts you to paste it).
                                                 Use --machine if the link has no machine id; add --ssh if the hub is reachable only over SSH.
                                                 --proxy <url> first saves an outbound HTTP(S) proxy for this computer, as persona-link proxy does.
  persona-link pair --listen [<listen address>] [--addr <address>]…
                                                 Passive mode (let the hub connect): listen locally (default :18663) and print a link to paste
                                                 into the hub admin page (valid for 10 minutes, one use only); --addr sets an address for the hub.
  persona-link mode [active|passive] [--listen <listen address>]
                                                 Show or change the mode: active connects to the hub; passive lets the hub connect.
                                                 Each mode keeps its own pairing, so switching back does not require pairing again.
  persona-link install [--pair <link>|-] [--machine <id>] [--ssh <server> [--ssh-target <address:port>] [--ssh-always|--no-ssh-always]] [--proxy <url>]
                    [--listen [<listen address>]] [--addr <address>]… [--node-bin <path> | --personad <path>] [--no-node]
                                                 Linux: install and start a systemd user service, then wait for the hub connection
                                                 (passive mode: wait for listening). --pair pairs first (active); --listen selects passive mode
                                                 and prints a pairing link if needed. Install the resident node service if missing (--no-node skips it).
                                                 Without systemd, print alternatives.
                                                 Mac: install the launchd user agent com.persona.link. The standalone Link package also installs
                                                 persona-node; the Electron desktop setup window can call this command.
                                                 Windows: install the scheduled task “Persona Link”, which starts at sign-in and restarts the
                                                 resident node and persona-link when they exit; --personad replaces personad.exe each time.
  persona-link node install [--node-bin <path> | --personad <path>] | switch [--to personad] | status [--json] | uninstall
                                                 Manage the resident node (node --attach) service: Linux systemd user service personad-node;
                                                 Mac launchd agent com.persona.node. An existing service is left unchanged.
                                                 Run the device's own ~/.persona/bin/persona-node when available, otherwise personad.
                                                 --node-bin detects which program was provided; --personad treats it as personad.
                                                 switch changes an installed service to persona-node (--to personad changes back), keeping
                                                 the old service file until the new node answers and restoring it if it does not.
  persona-link plugin status|install|uninstall|on|off [--json]
                                                 The Persona plugin for Claude Code, which the resident node carries and keeps installed at the user scope
                                                 (automatically on Mac and Windows). status checks it; install installs or updates it now; uninstall removes it
                                                 and turns the automatic install off; on / off turn only the automatic install on or off. New Claude Code
                                                 sessions load it; open ones keep what they loaded.
  persona-link discover [--wait <seconds>] [--json]    Discover hubs on the LAN (mDNS); exit 0 if one is heard, otherwise 1
  persona-link status [--json]                    Show mode, link, hub, local node, and background service status; exit 0 when connected
                                                 (passive mode: listening), otherwise 1
  persona-link reconnect                            Ask the running connector to reconnect immediately (also on Windows; used by desktop setup)
  persona-link logs [-f] [-n <lines>]              Show the log (~/.persona/link.log); -f follows it
  persona-link uninstall [--purge]                Stop and remove the systemd user service (Windows: scheduled task); --purge also removes credentials,
                                                 state, logs, the connector's TLS identity, and ~/.persona/bin/persona-link
  persona-link run [--parent] [--log <file>]      Keep the link running in the foreground and write one JSON status per line to standard output.
                                                 --parent: exit when standard input closes (for a compatible older parent process's console).
                                                 --log: write logs to this file (rotate at 1 MB), not standard error
  persona-link name [<new name>|--reset]           Show or change this computer's name on the hub (shown in the app, web, and admin views; id unchanged).
                                                 Ask the running, connected persona-link to ask the hub; --reset restores the id
  persona-link ssh [<server> | --off] [--target <address:port>] [--always|--no-always] [--test]
                                                 Show, set, or remove the SSH tunnel for active mode ([user@]host[:port] or a ~/.ssh/config alias;
                                                 by default, forward to 127.0.0.1:<TLS port> from the pairing link).
                                                 --always uses only the tunnel, --off removes it, and --test tests the connection
  persona-link proxy [<url> | --off | --env]
                                                 Show or set the outbound HTTP(S) proxy for active mode (http[s]://[user:password@]host:port).
                                                 Direct addresses are tried first; --off uses no proxy, not even HTTPS_PROXY or ALL_PROXY;
                                                 --env goes back to those environment variables (the default)
  persona-link address add <address>                 Add a hub candidate address manually (https://domain:port, or domain)
  persona-link address remove <address>              Remove a manually added address
  persona-link version [-v]                    Show the version; -v adds the release channel and build number

Signals (Linux, Mac): SIGUSR1 checks the link immediately after a network change; SIGUSR2 disconnects and reconnects. Windows uses named events with the same names (sent by reconnect).

windows_service_unregistered: Background service: scheduled task “{task}” is gone ({path} remains): run persona-link install again
windows_task_installed: Installed and started scheduled task “{task}” ({path}): starts when you sign in to Windows, restarts {programs} within seconds after exit, opens no window; logs are in {log}.
windows_task_removed: Stopped and removed scheduled task “{task}” (the resident node and persona-link stopped with it).
windows_user_unknown: Cannot determine the current Windows user, so the scheduled task cannot be installed
plugin_auto_off: Automatic install and updates: off (persona-link plugin on turns them on)
plugin_failed: The resident node could not check the Claude Code plugin: {error}
plugin_new_sessions: Claude Code reads plugins when a session starts: the change reaches new sessions; sessions already open keep what they loaded (/reload-plugins in a terminal session applies it now).
plugin_no_node: No resident node here ({path} is missing). The Claude Code plugin comes with the node: install it first (persona-link install).
plugin_node_too_old: The resident node program ({path}) cannot manage the Claude Code plugin: update the node first (Redeploy on the Machines page).
plugin_state_claude_missing: Claude Code plugin: no Claude Code on this computer (install it and start it once); nothing to install into
plugin_state_disabled: Claude Code plugin: turned off in Claude Code; Persona leaves it off (persona-link plugin install turns it back on)
plugin_state_error: Claude Code plugin: the last check failed: {error}
plugin_state_outdated: Claude Code plugin: version {version} installed; this node carries {bundled}
plugin_state_unavailable: Claude Code plugin: this node build carries no plugin
plugin_word_removed: removed in Claude Code; Persona leaves it removed (persona-link plugin install puts it back)
